checks_run.expected: Either the finding is Low, non-mandatory, latent and not a DG5 regression (accept), or it breaks a DG5 acceptance text, a financial result or access control (keep open).
checks_run.actual: Confirmed: fetchAllPages loops 20 pages of 100 and returns a silent prefix (queries.ts:104-119), whereas useAllTransformations throws after 1000 pages. The transformation-list callers in the finding already existed at DG4 e70ac02 (traceability/api.ts useReadableTransformations; benefits/api.ts:314), so this is not a regression. CompleteWithOutput.tsx:37 is a DG5 caller. The helper has 169 non-test callers. No DG5 acceptance text needs more than 2000 rows, and server-side totals are unaffected. The domain probe shows 2000/2150 in en and ar. Decision: ACCEPTED_OBSERVATION. The DG6 fix is to be scoped to fetchAllPages itself, with the rationale in the verifications sidecar. No new finding: the wider scope has the same root cause.

summary: PASS on candidate sha256:33188e9e... (2194 files, source 12dc33e), the same candidate my round-7 record reviewed. It was confirmed from the committed source at the start and the end, and in a complete clone. HEAD's id differs only because D-183 was appended to decisions.md after the freeze; the validator recomputes from the source commit. No new finding. All three open Low, non-mandatory findings are accepted as observations, each with a DG6 fix: F-DG5-125, the silent 2000-row cap, which is latent, existed at DG4, and needs a fix in fetchAllPages itself, which has 169 callers; F-DG5-150, the root note's overflow with an unbroken name, which is cosmetic, unchanged since DG4 and tied to a DG6-final requirement; F-DG5-151, the unsound wait in the health-check e2e, which is a test defect: the product always sent the current If-Match. The single D-182 failure is disclosed and its cause stays unestablished. The historical validators for DG4 to DG1 and the DG5 register rules pass. The 78 requirements rest on my round-7 execution on this same candidate.
